City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
September 4, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:05 p.m. , on September 4, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on August 30, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
William P. Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.
CS2.
Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
CS3.
Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission Viejo v. the State of California, Case No. 34 2012 8000 1203.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Leckness arrived at 6:07 p.m.)
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council did not address item CS1 and it will be re-calendared at a future meeting. For item CS2, the City Council received information and will consider giving staff further direction in the future. For item CS3, the Council received an update and an indication of the range of authority the City may have for bringing the matter to settlement however, there was no definitive action from Closed Session.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Proclaim the Month of September 2012, as World Alzheimer’s Awareness Month
Mayor Ury presented the proclamation to Andrew Eng, Outreach and Advocacy Coordinator, Alzheimer’s Association Orange County Chapter.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Ed Sachs, M.V.: discussed Proposition 32 which will discourage special interest funds for politicians and government officials. He stated that he believes it will be a game changer in California and he asked the City Council to adopt a Resolution supporting Proposition 32.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that past City Councils had an opportunity, many times, to get work done on the Nadadores complex and it has been pushed off for a variety of reasons. She noted that the City should fulfill its contract and get the work done as soon as possible and the Nadadores should pay their fair share of the utilities.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: referred to the tennis and aquatics center project and stated that it did not come in under budget. He noted that a resident of Casta del Sol misinformed Casta residents about the budget and they should verify the information they received.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that she attended the recent WWII Veteran recognition at the Murray center and it was another great event. She also thanked the City Council for the newly remodeled Marguerite Recreation Complex and she stated that the slopes on the adjacent property now need updating. Mrs. Bucknum asked the City Council to take steps to gain an easement along the greenbelt so that the Oso trail can be completed for the purpose of maintaining the slopes, beautification, and for passive recreation.
Matt Trudell, M.V.: speaking in defense of Council Member Schlicht, he stated that her points on the Special Fire Protection Area at the last meeting were right on and he believes her statements were more accurate than the opinions of others.
Robert D. Breton, M.V.: congratulated Recreation and Community Services staff for maximizing use of the Potocki Center. He also thanked the City for the magnificent Symphony in the Cities program and for completing the Library’s Community Room. Mr. Breton informed residents that the Readers’ Festival will be held on October 14, 2012, he thanked the Council for the newly improved tennis center, and lastly, he suggested that the City reactivate the wonderful tradition of a St. Patrick’s Day parade in March 2013 for the City’s 25 th anniversary.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that he stands by his opinion on the Special Fire Protection Area as he stated it two weeks ago. He noted that the Orange County Grand Jury investigated 58 entities in Orange County and Mission Viejo came out with one A and two DD ratings. He suggested that the City review the Grand Jury recommendations and comply with them.
Helen Workun, M.V.: thanked the Council and the 7-11 manager for agreeing to change the hours of the new store on Marguerite Parkway from 5 a.m. to midnight and she thanked Mayor Pro Tem Reardon for placing the item on the last agenda. Ms. Workun stated, for the record, that she is opposed to digital signage on the Kaleidoscope building and she asked the City Council to make sure that the issue of digital signage is gone forever.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 2 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Before approval of item 6, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon commended the Public Works Department for coming in under budget on the Avery Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation project from Camino Capistrano to Marguerite Parkway (CIP 837.)
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
3.
Check Register dated August 10, 2012 in the amount of $1,309,816.68
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated August 17, 2012 in the amount of $566,902.81
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Check Register dated August 24, 2012 in the amount of $1,160,768.21
Ratified the accompanying check register.
6.
Avery Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation, Camino Capistrano to Marguerite Parkway (CIP 837) - Notice of Completion
(1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
7.
La Paz Roadway and Bridge Widening Improvements (CIP 756/761)
(1) Authorized the approval of Change Order 4 to Parsons Transportation Group, Inc., in the amount of $191,695 for additional design services; and (2) adopted Resolution 12-53 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 761.
8.
Agreement for Oversight Board Legal Services (Harper & Burns LLP)
Approved Agreement for Oversight Board Legal Services with Harper & Burns LLP in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00 for each six-month ROPS.
9.
Trustee Services for ICMA Retirement Corporation Section 457 Deferred Compensation Plan
Adopted Resolution No. 12-54 Approving the Appointment of Wilmington Trust Retirement and Institutional Services Company ("Wilmington Trust") to Provide Passive-Directed Trustee Services to the City’s ICMA-RC 401(a) and 457(b) Governmental Deferred Compensation Plans.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
2.
City Council Minutes
Council Member Schlicht asked that the Minutes be amended to reflect, on page 9, that it was Mayor Pro Tem Reardon who stated that the real estate signs would be an advertisement. Council Member Schlicht did not make that comment but rather, she noted that she felt the signs would compete with the tenant signs.
On page 13, Council Member Schlicht asked that the Minutes be amended to reflect that the Council, by consensus, directed that Agendas and Minutes of the City’s standing committees be posted on the City web site.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 20, 2012, as amended.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
10.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that OCFA needs more transparency to ensure that the Grand Jury is given a proper and complete response regarding disclosure and compensation.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
11.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA and he notified his colleagues that Transportation Corridor Agencies CEO Tom Margro has resigned.
12.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
13.
Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board
City Manager Wilberg presented the report.
City Attorney's Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
14.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley congratulated Casta del Sol on its 40th anniversary celebration. She stated that it is a beautiful community and the residents of Casta del Sol have been good neighbors for the past 40 years. Council Member Kelley announced that the Marine Adoption Committee is looking for support for shoe box care packages which are sent overseas to deployed service men and women. There is a list on line and fliers in the foyer which outline the items that can be included in the boxes. She noted that receiving those boxes is a highlight for the deployed Marines and they are so appreciative of the gesture. In addition, the Marine Corps birthday ball is approaching and the Marine Adoption Committee is seeking clean, formal gowns or prom dresses for the Marine wives. Lastly, Council Member Kelley drew attention to the after school enrichment programs at the Potocki Center. The classes began last year and they have been tremendously popular. The program will continue this year for middle school students, grades 6-8, and information is available on the City’s web site.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness announced that he attended a recent one man art show at the Murray Center and a Quinceañera was being held in an adjacent room. He noted how impressed he is by the variety of programs and events that are held at the Center. He also attended the opening of the newly renovated Marguerite tennis complex and he encouraged residents to stop by and see the fabulous facility and the pro purple tennis courts. Council Member Leckness outlined his attendance at the WWII recognition ceremony where the Marine Corps band from Camp Pendleton played. He stated that it was very powerful to be that close to the band and the tuba player in particular.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht thanked residents Matt Trudell and Stephen Wontrobski for their comments earlier in the evening and for supporting her position on the Special Fire Protection Area. She reiterated that she thinks disclosure will be a problem for the residents in the SFPA. Council Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at the 40th anniversary for Casta del Sol and she thanked the community for the invitation. She also attended the WWII Veterans recognition where she enjoyed walking among the tables and talking to the veterans. She expressed her thanks to the WWII vets and stated that we are here because of them. Council Member Schlicht asked that the American Legion be part of the next Veterans Day ceremony and the Memorial Day ceremony next May. She noted that the American Legion is vital to our community and one of the oldest traditions in the Nation. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from Ronald Reagan: “Freedom is the right to question and change the established way of doing things.”
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon discussed her attendance at the WWII recognition event where there were over 170 Veterans in attendance. She thanked the Veterans Recognition Committee for doing an outstanding job and she noted that without the veterans who were recognized, we would not be here. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon encouraged residents to attend a fundraiser for the Special Olympics at PKSA Karate Studio on Saturday, September 8, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. She also affirmed that she stands by what she has said on the Special Fire Protection Area and if it turns out she has made a mistake, she will publicly apologize and work her hardest to correct that mistake. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon stated that there is an epidemic with young people who are using prescription drugs, getting hooked on them, and losing their lives as a result. She announced the screening of a new film on the subject entitled Behind the Orange Curtain which will be shown to an audience of 400 people on October 4, 2012, at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon shared a short trailer of the film and she encouraged residents to make plans to attend the screening and become educated about this very real problem.
Mayor Ury
15.
Mission Viejo Marguerite Recreation Center - Aquatics Complex Rehabilitation
Mayor Ury presented his report.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that the project should be done quickly but the price needs to be closely evaluated. She encouraged the Council to look at the contract with the Nadadores, evaluate the surveys that have been done on the subject, do some public outreach and involve the residents.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: announced that Council Member Schlicht first brought this item before the City Council in June 2011 and he stated that Mayor Ury is trying to gain favor by placing it on the agenda now, before the upcoming election.
Jim Montrella, M.V.: expressed support for the recommended action and for the rehabilitation of the Aquatics complex.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: expressed support for the proposed aquatics complex rehabilitation.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct staff to budget funds to begin the design of the improvements to the Aquatics Complex.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Mayor Ury announced that he was very disappointed that he was unable to attend the Casta del Sol 40th anniversary party. He was in Phoenix, Arizona watching his son play football for Santa Margarita High School and they won the game. Mayor Ury discussed his attendance at the WWII Veterans celebration and he noted that he had a wonderful time listening to the vets’ stories and what a treasure it was to spend time with them.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 7:56 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Bill Klimek to Monday, September 17, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of September 17, 2012
